title: Bram and the Vector
premise: Ivo Brightwater investigates impossible accidents along the long route between the Earth Fleet and the Breakaway Colonies, two fleets that severed contact decades ago. When a ship that never flew appears on her manifest carrying a passenger named Bram — a man who officially does not exist — she discovers both fleets are being manipulated toward war by a hidden syndicate profiting from the silence between them. To stop it, Ivo must keep alive a forged transmission loop, a lie that convinces each fleet the other still wants peace, while hunting the syndicate's agent inside her own chain of command. In the end, she exposes the conspiracy at the relay station where the last true message from Earth is stored, chooses to broadcast the truth even though it may shatter the fragile peace her lie preserved, and finds belonging not in either fleet but among the route-walkers who keep the line between worlds.
about_author: Ada Montrose is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years auditing cargo claims before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted lightship off the northern coast, where she collects obsolete radio equipment and answers letters from readers by post.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ivo Brightwater, POV. Investigating a cargo hauler that burned in vacuum with no cause, Ivo finds a passenger manifest listing a ship that was never registered and a name — Bram — attached to no fleet database. The emotional beat: professional unease curdling into obsession as the impossible refuses to stay filed.

chapters.title: Long Route Rules
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. She travels the relay chain between Earth Fleet and the Breakaway Colonies, establishing the world: silent fleets, neutral stations, route-walkers who carry messages for pay. A colleague warns her to drop the ghost manifest. Beat: loneliness of the job, and the first hint someone is watching her inquiries.

chapters.title: Bram
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. At Meridian Station she meets Bram himself — calm, unregistered, carrying an antique data spool he claims is family property. He knows details of the burned hauler no outsider could. Beat: wary fascination; two investigators circling the same impossible accident from opposite sides.

chapters.title: The Spool
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. His perspective reveals he is a Breakaway archivist smuggled out with proof that Earth's final transmission loop — the peace signal both fleets still monitor — was tampered with years ago. Beat: his fear that Ivo is Fleet intelligence, and his decision to trust her anyway.

chapters.title: Actuarial Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Back-tracing the hauler's insurance history, she finds seven 'impossible accidents' on the same route, all settled quietly by the same underwriter, Corvane Mutual. Beat: the cold pleasure of pattern recognition giving way to dread at its size.

chapters.title: The Underwriter
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. She interviews Corvane's regional director, Vess Okonkwo, who is charming, helpful, and lying about everything. Ivo leaves with a copy of a settlement file and a tail she can't shake. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; power wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: What the Loop Says
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram decodes part of the spool: the peace transmission both fleets obey is a recording, maintained by a private relay consortium — Corvane's parent. Whoever controls the loop controls the war footing of two civilizations. Beat: vertigo at the scale of the deception.

chapters.title: Route-Walkers
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. She takes refuge with the route-walkers, an informal guild of couriers who owe her old favors. Their leader, Sefa, agrees to hide Bram but demands Ivo learn what the guild really is to her. Beat: warmth and belonging offered, and resisted.

chapters.title: A Death on Meridian
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. The Meridian stationmaster who certified the ghost manifest dies in another impossible accident — hull breach, sealed compartment, no cause. Ivo realizes she isn't investigating accidents; she's walking their rehearsal list. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Fleet Interest
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Fleet Security officer Dain Rusk contacts her, offering protection and resources — if she hands over Bram. He seems honest, which makes it worse. Beat: divided loyalty; the law offering justice at the price of a person.

chapters.title: The Lie Begins
chapters.summary: Bram and Ivo, alternating. They discover the loop is degrading — Earth's last genuine message ends in weeks — and Corvane plans to replace it with a forged signal provoking a border incident. Together they begin forging a counter-transmission: a lie that holds the fleets apart. Beat: complicity; two people choosing deception as mercy.

chapters.title: Settlement Terms
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. She confronts Okonkwo with the settlement files. He doesn't deny it; he offers her a partnership — wealth, immunity, a seat at the table. Beat: temptation rendered politely; corruption explained as simply good business.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. She declines and walks out knowing Okonkwo will now kill her. Rusk shadows her, ambiguous. Beat: fear without regret; the point of no return crossed quietly.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. The route-walkers debate sheltering Ivo's conspiracy. Sefa reveals the guild once served both fleets as neutral mail and was broken by Corvane's predecessors. Beat: old wounds; belonging redefined as shared injury rather than shared blood.

chapters.title: The Relay Chain
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram maps the physical relays that carry the loop and identifies the master node at Station Erebus, inside contested space. Reaching it means crossing both fleets' patrol lines. Beat: daunted planning; hope taking the shape of a route.

chapters.title: Rusk's File
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Rusk shows her evidence Fleet command already knows the loop is fake — and has decided a controlled war is cheaper than admitting it. Beat: betrayal by institutions; justice visibly absent from the law.

chapters.title: Passenger Manifest
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Using her investigator credentials, Ivo forges travel papers placing herself and Bram on a legitimate freighter — echoing the ghost manifest that started everything. Beat: ironic satisfaction; becoming the forgery she chased.

chapters.title: Crossing the Line
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. The freighter slips through the Breakaway picket line; Bram faces a colony patrol officer who knew his father. He talks them past — barely. Beat: home that won't have him; identity as negotiation.

chapters.title: Accident, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Corvane attempts to destroy the freighter with the same impossible-accident method used on the hauler. Ivo recognizes the signature mid-crisis and vents the right compartment in time. Beat: competence as survival; her trade saving lives instead of pricing them.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Among the freighter crew, Bram learns the burned hauler's dead included a Corvane auditor who tried to blow the whistle. He and Ivo hold a small memorial in the cargo bay. Beat: mourning as commitment; the cost made personal.

chapters.title: Erebus Approach
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. They reach Station Erebus disguised as salvage contractors. The master node sits behind Corvane security and a legal quarantine neither fleet will violate. Beat: coiled anticipation; the plan's hinge approaching.

chapters.title: Okonkwo Arrives
chapters.summary: Okonkwo, POV (first antagonist view). He comes to Erebus to oversee the loop replacement personally, bringing Rusk — revealed as his paid informant. Beat: villainy at ease; the machinery of power confident and bored.

chapters.title: Inside the Node
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram infiltrates the node via maintenance tunnels while Ivo creates a diversion with a staged insurance inspection. He reaches the archive holding Earth's true final message. Beat: awe and sorrow hearing humanity's real last words.

chapters.title: The True Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Bram plays her the authentic loop: not a peace treaty but a plea — Earth asking both fleets, in plain language, to talk. Both fleets have been obeying a corrupted fragment for years. Beat: devastating clarity; the lie they must now tell is truer than the truth in circulation.

chapters.title: Compromise
chapters.summary: Ivo and Bram, alternating. They craft the forged continuation: a loop extension that keeps the fleets talking long enough for direct contact to be rebuilt. It requires broadcasting from Erebus continuously — meaning someone must stay at the node. Beat: quiet sacrifice taking shape.

chapters.title: Rusk's Choice
chapters.summary: Rusk, POV. Ordered to arrest Ivo, Rusk reviews her evidence overnight and realizes Fleet command authorized the cover-up. He burns his orders. Beat: a lawman discovering justice outside the law; redemption earned reluctantly.

chapters.title: Quarantine Breach
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Corvane detects the intrusion and locks down Erebus, venting sections methodically — another impossible accident, this time aimed at everyone. Ivo organizes the station's contractors into an evacuation that shouldn't work. Beat: leadership under pressure; ordinary people against corporate arithmetic.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Console
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Face to face with Okonkwo in the node chamber, she offers him the only deal she has: testimony and exile in exchange for standing down. He refuses; Rusk arrests him instead, on charges that will never stick. Beat: climax of wills; the law arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram initiates the forged loop extension as Corvane saboteurs cut power. The transmission catches on backup capacitors and holds. Both fleets' nav systems register the continued signal. Beat: triumph trembling on failure; the lie going live.

chapters.title: The Price of the Node
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Keeping the broadcast stable requires manual cycling every few hours — indefinitely. Ivo volunteers to stay; Bram refuses to leave her. Beat: love declared through logistics; sacrifice negotiated into shared burden.

chapters.title: Two Fleets Answer
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Days later, both fleets send inquiry pings to Erebus — the first direct contact in forty years. The route-walkers arrive to establish a permanent courier line. Beat: vindication and wonder; silence ending.

chapters.title: Hearings
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Summoned to a joint tribunal, Ivo testifies, withholding the forgery and claiming the loop was restored. Justice is partial, imperfect, hers to shape. Beat: moral weight carried alone; peace built on a protected lie.

chapters.title: Corvane Unwound
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. The route-walkers release Corvane's internal archives guild-wide; underwriters collapse, Okonkwo's patrons scatter. Not law — consequence. Beat: rough justice; satisfaction shadowed by what it cost.

chapters.title: Bram's Archive
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram donates the spool to a new joint archive on Meridian, the station where he was nearly killed. He is granted dual registration — a status that didn't exist before. Beat: belonging formalized; the man who didn't exist now on every manifest.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Restored
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo resumes investigations, but now the route has traffic, embassies, noise. An impossible accident lands on her desk — small, human, solvable. Beat: return to scale; purpose renewed in ordinary work.

chapters.title: What the Loop Costs
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Maintenance shifts at Erebus rotate among volunteers now, but Ivo keeps the anniversary shift alone, listening to Earth's true last words. Beat: elegy; memory as duty.

chapters.title: Rusk's Report
chapters.summary: Rusk, POV. Rusk, reassigned to the joint commission, quietly buries the anomaly in the loop records — protecting Ivo's lie forever. Beat: complicity accepted; the lawman now keeper of the secret.

chapters.title: Manifest Entry
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram files a new ship registration — a courier vessel named after the hauler that burned — with two names on the manifest: Brightwater and Bram. Beat: tenderness in paperwork; a future written in the format that began the story.

chapters.title: The Vector
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Standing watch at Erebus, Ivo reflects that a vector has direction and magnitude — and so did every choice since the ghost manifest. The fleets speak; the lie holds; the route continues. Beat: resolution; peace understood as something maintained, not won.

chapters.title: Next of Kin
chapters.summary: Ivo and Bram, alternating closing pages. They take the new courier out on its first run, carrying mail between worlds that finally answer. A young route-walker asks Ivo why she stayed in the business of accidents. She says someone has to read the manifests closely. Beat: belonging found; the story closing on forward motion.
